newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FEHR HAS THREE-STROKE LEAD AFTER SECOND ROUND IN LAS VEGAS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FEHR HAS THREE-STROKE LEAD AFTER SECOND ROUND IN LAS VEGAS.

text.p: Rick Fehr matched a PGA Tour record for lowest 36-hole score with a 10-under par 62 at the TPC at Summerlin for a three-shot lead after two rounds of the Las Vegas Invitational on Thursday.
Fehr's 126 after two rounds tied the Tour record held by John Cook, Tommy Bolt and Paul Azinger. Cook's total came earlier this year at the St. Jude Classic in Memphis.

Fehr, who shot a 7-under-par 64 at the Las Vegas Hilton Country Club on Wednesday in the first day of the 90-hole event, was 9-under after 11 holes on Thursday and said he began to think of shooting a 59.

"It's pretty difficult not to think about shooting 59 when you're 9-under after 11, but shooting 59 was not my goal," said Fehr, who missed a number of makeable birdie putts over the final seven hole and had an eagle attempt slide inches past on the 16th.

Despite Fehr's brilliance, there are nine players within six shots of his lead. Ronnie Black fired a 65 and Fred Funk had a 66 to tie for second at 129. Defending champion Jim Furyk shot a 64 and is alone in fourth at 130.

"It's kind of scary to play the way I did for the first two days and not have a big lead," Fehr said. "I should have like a 6-shot lead. But that's typical of this tournament. The courses are in great shape and when you have the world's best players playing on courses this well kept, you're going to have some low scores."

Heralded rookie Tiger Woods, who shot a disappointing 1-under 70 at the Las Vegas Hilton Country Club Wednesday, played himself back into contention by firing a 9-under 63. Woods is in a five-way tie for 11th at 133 with Davis Love III, Fred Couples, Glen Day and Frank Lickliter.
